title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From MD Anderson Cancer Center in 2026
summary: Every MD Anderson form, phone number, fax, and address you need to request medical records in 2026, plus the authorization rules and routing details that keep legal requests from stalling.
body_markdown:
MD Anderson reported serving nearly 200,000 patients and families in FY2025, so its records turn up regularly in personal injury, medical malpractice, and wrongful death matters. For legal professionals working those cases, knowing which form to submit, where to send it, and which details trigger a rejection helps avoid preventable delays. This guide covers the contact details, form requirements, and procedural steps you need. For firms handling volume,[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-powered retrieval that validates authorizations before submission and manages persistent follow-up until records arrive.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


MD Anderson does not publish a fixed completion time for legal requests; its[Notice of Privacy Practices](https://www.mdanderson.org/about-md-anderson/business-legal/legal-and-policy/legal-statements/notice-of-privacy-practices.html) states it will take action on certain written access requests within 15 days


-


The standard authorization is[Form INS999544](https://www.mdanderson.org/content/dam/mdanderson/documents/patients-and-family/becoming-our-patient/services-and-amenities/Patient%20Authorization%20Disclosure%20Form.pdf) , two pages, revised April 20, 2026


-


The authorization expires at the later of one year after signature or the date or event specified on the form


-


Two current MD Anderson sources give different ROI mailing addresses, so verify before mailing


-


Medical images and radiology reports go to the Film Library at 713-792-6210, though the authorization also has a Diagnostic Imaging section


-


Billing records are available in paper format only, per the form


-

## **Understanding MD Anderson's Medical Records Request Process**


MD Anderson's Health Information Management department handles record requests through a centralized Release of Information office. That central contact covers the main Houston campus and the regional locations in The Woodlands, Sugar Land, League City, and West Houston, but MD Anderson doesn't publish language guaranteeing that one authorization automatically captures every record from every location. When a patient received care at more than one facility, identify the relevant facilities and treatment dates in the request.


The ROI office accepts requests by[fax, email, mail](https://www.mdanderson.org/patients-family/becoming-our-patient/services-amenities/medical-records.html) , or in-person drop-off. It reviews each authorization for completeness before beginning retrieval, so an incomplete form delays the request before processing starts.


Incomplete or defective authorizations are a leading preventable cause of rejected requests. For firms running several MD Anderson matters at once, the manual work of tracking submissions, chasing pending requests, and verifying completeness adds up fast.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) manages provider outreach across calls, faxes, emails, and portals until the requested materials arrive, giving your team visibility into completed outreach and next required actions.


## **Essential MD Anderson Medical Records Release Forms**


### **Primary Authorization Form Requirements**


[Form INS999544](https://www.mdanderson.org/content/dam/mdanderson/documents/patients-and-family/becoming-our-patient/services-and-amenities/Patient%20Authorization%20Disclosure%20Form.pdf) , "Authorization for the Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information," is MD Anderson's standard authorization for release of protected health information. It is a two-page document, currently revised April 20, 2026. Additional documentation may be required when a personal representative signs.


**The form asks for this patient information:**


-


Patient full legal name, ideally matching hospital records


-


Date of birth


-


Complete mailing address and telephone number


-


Patient number or Medical Record Number (MRN)


**And this recipient information:**


-


Law firm or attorney name


-


Complete firm address


-


Phone and fax numbers


-


Email address for electronic delivery


### **Record Types Available for Request**


The authorization includes checkboxes for specific record categories. Common litigation selections:


-


Entire Legal Medical Record


-


Abstract of Record


-


Consultation notes, progress notes, and discharge summary


-


History and Physical (H&P)


-


Operative reports and laboratory testing


-


Pathology records, including slides and blocks


-


Diagnostic imaging notes and reports, and diagnostic imaging in CD/DVD or paper format


-


Billing records (paper format only, per the form)


A narrower request may reduce the volume of material produced, though MD Anderson doesn't publish a guaranteed time or cost reduction based on scope. As a matter of general practice, malpractice matters often call for the complete legal medical record, but what's needed depends on the issues, discovery strategy, experts, and governing law rather than any MD Anderson requirement.


Codes Health helps identify which record types matter for a given case type, so documentation stays complete without unnecessary breadth.


## **Navigating HIPAA Requirements for MD Anderson Records**


### **Authorization Signatures and Legal Representatives**


For an authorization-based request, the authorization must be valid and signed by the patient or an appropriate personal representative. HIPAA also permits or requires disclosures in certain circumstances without a patient authorization, including specified judicial and administrative processes, so an authorization isn't the only mechanism in every proceeding.


The form provides for signature by the patient or a personal representative, and lists Parent, Guardian, or Other (specify) as the representative's authority. A power of attorney holder, executor, administrator, or other representative may qualify under applicable law, but those aren't separate categories printed on the form. The signer specifies their authority.


For a deceased patient, the person requesting or authorizing disclosure may need to establish legal authority to act for the patient or estate. Under[HHS guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/under-hipaa-when-can-a-family-member/index.html) , the decedent's personal representative is generally an executor, administrator, or another person authorized under applicable law. Family relationship alone does not confer the personal representative's full access rights. MD Anderson may require documentation establishing the signer's authority, so confirm what's needed with the ROI office for the specific circumstances.


The authorization must be signed and dated. If there's any question about an electronic signature format, confirm it with the ROI office before submitting.


### **Sensitive Information Acknowledgment**


The authorization includes language expressly authorizing disclosure of specified sensitive information, which may include data related to:


-


AIDS or HIV infection


-


Drug or alcohol abuse


-


Mental or behavioral health care


-


Psychiatric care, excluding psychotherapy notes


There's no separate signature block for this acknowledgment. The patient or personal representative signs the authorization on page 2.


### **Authorization Expiration Rules**


MD Anderson's current form states that the authorization expires at the[later of one year](https://www.mdanderson.org/content/dam/mdanderson/documents/patients-and-family/becoming-our-patient/services-and-amenities/Patient%20Authorization%20Disclosure%20Form.pdf) after signature or the date or event specified on the form. For litigation running long, plan to refresh authorizations rather than assume coverage.


The form also carries a re-disclosure warning: once disclosed, information may be re-disclosed by the recipient and may no longer be protected by federal privacy regulations.

## **Requesting Your Own Medical Records Online from MD Anderson**


MD Anderson patients can access records through[MyChart](https://my.mdanderson.org/) , which lets them view health summaries, test results, and clinical information, request medical records, handle prescription refills, and message care teams.


Adult MyChart users can grant proxy access to another adult with permission. MD Anderson describes this in terms of family members, friends, and others the patient trusts; its public materials don't specifically address attorney proxy access, so don't assume that route is available.


The information available in the portal may differ from a formally requested record set, so for litigation documentation, a formal ROI request remains the reliable path.


## **Retrieving Old or Archived Medical Records from MD Anderson**


### **Record Retention and Archive Access**


MD Anderson maintains records according to Texas retention requirements and institutional policies. Texas rules generally require hospitals to retain specified medical records for at least 10 years, while some categories, including imaging, carry different retention periods. Records may also be kept longer under institutional policy or a litigation hold.


For older treatment dates, contact the ROI office at 713-792-6710 to confirm availability before submitting a formal request.


### **Multi-Location Record Coordination**


MD Anderson operates[multiple locations](https://www.mdanderson.org/about-md-anderson/contact-us.html) across Texas:


-


Texas Medical Center, Houston (main campus)


-


West Houston: 713-563-9600


-


League City: 713-563-0670


-


Sugar Land: 281-566-1800


-


The Woodlands: 713-563-0050


MD Anderson publishes a centralized ROI contact, but when a patient received care at several locations, name the relevant facilities and treatment dates in the request rather than assuming one authorization sweeps everything up.


Codes Health uses provider and facility data to identify where records may exist, which matters for patients with long treatment histories across multiple locations.


## **Tips for a Smooth MD Anderson Medical Records Request**


### **Common Rejection Triggers to Avoid**


Incomplete or defective authorizations are a leading preventable cause of rejected requests. Common problems:


-


**Missing signature:** the form must be signed and dated


-


**Incorrect date range:** double-check case dates, or specify all dates if uncertain


-


**Expired authorization:** check the form's expiration terms before relying on an older signature


-


**Name mismatch:** the patient name should match hospital records, including maiden names or aliases


-


**Wrong route for imaging:** images and radiology reports go to the Film and Image Library


-


**Missing fields:** complete the patient and recipient information the form asks for


### **Processing Timeline Expectations**


MD Anderson doesn't publish a fixed completion time for standard legal requests on its current medical records page. Its Notice of Privacy Practices states that it will take action on certain written individual-access requests within 15 days, which is not the same as a delivery guarantee for attorney-requested records. Treat any internal deadline you set as a firm workflow practice, not an MD Anderson commitment.


### **Follow-Up Protocol**


If a request is pending, contact the ROI office at 713-792-6710 for status information. Have your submission date and method ready, confirm the authorization was received, and ask for an estimated completion date.

The form is the easy part at MD Anderson. What trips firms up sits around it: whether the signer's authority is documented the way MD Anderson wants it, whether the expiration was read as the later of the two dates rather than the earlier, and which of two official mailing addresses the envelope should carry. Imaging has its own phone number. ## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does MD Anderson retain medical records?**


MD Anderson follows Texas retention requirements and institutional policies. Texas rules generally require hospitals to retain specified medical records for at least 10 years, while some categories, including imaging, have different retention periods, and records may be held longer under institutional policy or a litigation hold. For older treatment dates, contact the ROI office at 713-792-6710 to confirm availability before submitting a formal request.


### **Can I request MD Anderson records for a deceased family member without being the executor?**


It depends on your legal authority, not your relationship. Under HIPAA, the decedent's personal representative is generally an executor, administrator, or another person authorized under applicable law to act for the decedent or estate; a family relationship alone doesn't confer those access rights. HIPAA separately permits certain limited disclosures to family members involved in the decedent's care or payment, which is not the same as obtaining a complete litigation record. Contact the MD Anderson Privacy Officer at privacy@mdanderson.org for requirements in your situation.


### **What are the fees for MD Anderson medical records?**


MD Anderson states that in some cases it charges for paper copies and publishes a Release of Information fee schedule, and its Notice of Privacy Practices notes that certain reasonable copying and delivery costs may be charged. It doesn't publish a guarantee of an advance cost breakdown on every request, so ask the ROI office about charges before submitting a large request.


### **How do I obtain pathology slides or tissue blocks from MD Anderson?**


Pathology slides and blocks have their own checkboxes on Form INS999544, so specify them in the pathology section of the authorization. For expert review in a malpractice matter, request both the pathology reports and the physical specimens. Confirm handling, shipping, and any associated charges with the ROI office, since MD Anderson doesn't publish those details.


### **What should I do if the records I received appear incomplete?**


Document what's missing and contact the ROI office at 713-792-6710, referencing your original request date and any confirmation details, then ask what's needed to obtain the items that should have been covered by your authorization. Any additional charges are for MD Anderson to determine. If the missing material is imaging, contact the Film and Image Library at 713-792-6210.
